about.heroSub: Pushing the boundaries of sound. Elevating artists. Creating legacy.
about.philosophy: Quantum Frequency Records is an independent label and creative platform built around artists, sounds and stories that do not need to fit inside a predetermined genre or commercial template.
about.mission: A home for artists, sounds and stories that refuse to exist inside the expected. We exist to discover, harness, partner and succeed — in that order, and without apology.
about.origin: QFR began as a simple observation: the most interesting music was happening between the lanes. Country next to industrial. Surf next to nu-metal. A DJ's 4AM protocol next to a fiddle. The label was built as a frequency, not a format — a place where those signals could occupy the same universe without being sanded into a brand-safe average.
about.artistFirst: The number one selling point is that the label is not greedy. Artists keep ownership of their own material. We do not push a corporate style to conform to, and we will not disrupt creativity to make a catalog look tidy.
about.beyondGenre: The roster intentionally spans country, country rock, punk, alternative, progressive and space rock, electronic, industrial, nu-metal, rap rock, psychedelic and indie sounds. That range is not a marketing trick. It is the point.
about.ai: Some catalog work at QFR is AI-created or AI-assisted where the label has approved that context. We treat those tools as instruments — visible, credited, and never a substitute for artist intent. When a work is machine-collaborative, we say so. When it is human to the bone, we say that too.
about.future: The next phase is a living universe: a store for physical and digital artifacts, live data for what is actually moving, and a CMS behind the same JSON bones that already run this site. New artists should be additions to the system — never a reason to duplicate the website.
about.quote: Every artist has a frequency. Our mission is helping the world hear it.

quotes.quote: They didn't ask us to become a genre. They asked the genre to make room.
Ownership is not a talking point here. It is the contract.
A label that treats silence like an instrument is a label I can work inside.

faqs.q: Do artists keep their masters and songs?
faqs.a: Yes. Ownership of material stays with the artist. QFR is a platform and a partner — not a landlord.

faqs.q: Do you force a house sound or brand template?
faqs.a: No. The roster spans country to industrial on purpose. We will not sand a song into a corporate average.

faqs.q: How do I submit music or a collaboration?
faqs.a: Use the contact form and choose Request Collaboration. Links, role, and a short note are enough to start.

faqs.q: Where can I buy merch or physical releases?
faqs.a: The store is coming online. Leave a suggestion via Contact, or follow the label socials for the drop.

faqs.q: Can I license a song or video?
faqs.a: Choose Request the Use of Content on the contact page and tell us which work, which artist, and how you want to use it.

faqs.q: Is some of the catalog AI-assisted?
faqs.a: Where that is true, we say so. Machines are instruments here — credited, never a substitute for artist intent.
